programs.title: Neurological Rehabilitation
programs.summary: Multidisciplinary care for people whose movement, balance, communication, cognition, or independence has been affected by a neurological condition.
who: Adults and children living with neurological diagnoses
People experiencing changes in movement, coordination, balance, speech, cognition, or daily function
Families and caregivers seeking coordinated outpatient support
goals: Increase participation at home and in the community

programs.title: Brain Injury & Stroke Rehabilitation
programs.summary: A coordinated program addressing mobility, communication, cognition, self-care, and participation after stroke or acquired brain injury.
who: People recovering from traumatic or acquired brain injury
Families adapting to cognitive, communication, or functional changes
goals: Support return to home, school, work, or community life

programs.title: Balance, Gait & Fall Prevention
programs.summary: Evaluation and treatment for walking difficulty, dizziness, balance loss, fall risk, and reduced confidence with movement.
who: People who have fallen or are afraid of falling
People with unsteady walking or reduced mobility
People with dizziness or vestibular symptoms
People who may need an assistive device
goals: Increase independence at home and in the community

programs.title: Pediatric Rehabilitation
programs.summary: Physical, occupational, speech, feeding, and developmental support for children and their families.
who: Children with developmental, motor, sensory, communication, or feeding needs
Children recovering from injury or illness
Families seeking coordinated therapy and practical guidance
goals: Help children participate more fully at home, school, and play

programs.title: Pain, Orthopedic & Post-Surgical Rehabilitation
programs.summary: Focused rehabilitation for pain, injury, surgery recovery, and musculoskeletal limitations that affect movement and daily life.
who: People recovering after surgery or injury
People with persistent back, neck, joint, or extremity pain
People whose pain limits work, mobility, sleep, or daily activity
goals: Improve movement and tolerance for activity
Support a safe return to work or recreation

services.title: Physical Therapy
services.summary: Care focused on movement, mobility, strength, balance, walking, endurance, coordination, and pain-limited function.

services.title: Occupational Therapy
services.summary: Care focused on the practical skills needed for everyday life at home, school, work, and in the community.
helps: Dressing, bathing, grooming, and meal preparation
Return to school, work, or community roles

services.title: Speech-Language Therapy
services.summary: Care addressing communication, speech, language, cognition, voice, feeding, chewing, and swallowing.

conditions.title: Stroke
conditions.summary: A stroke may affect movement, balance, speech, language, cognition, swallowing, vision, and everyday independence. Rehabilitation is organized around the particular functions that changed.

conditions.title: Traumatic Brain Injury
conditions.summary: A traumatic brain injury may affect physical ability, thinking, communication, behavior, endurance, and participation in daily life. Care should be individualized to the person’s current needs and goals.

conditions.title: Spinal Cord Injury
conditions.summary: Spinal cord injury can affect movement, sensation, mobility, self-care, endurance, and participation. Rehabilitation may focus on safe mobility, adaptive strategies, equipment, and practical independence.

conditions.title: Parkinson’s Disease & Movement Disorders
conditions.summary: Movement disorders may affect walking, balance, coordination, speech, voice, swallowing, and the speed or ease of everyday tasks.

conditions.title: Multiple Sclerosis & Progressive Neurological Conditions
conditions.summary: Progressive neurological conditions may cause changing difficulties with mobility, fatigue, balance, cognition, communication, or daily activity. Rehabilitation can adapt over time.

conditions.title: Cerebral Palsy & Pediatric Neurological Conditions
conditions.summary: Pediatric neurological conditions may affect movement, coordination, posture, communication, feeding, sensory processing, and participation in home and school routines.

conditions.title: Balance Disorders, Dizziness & Fall Risk
conditions.summary: Balance problems may come from neurological, vestibular, strength, medication, vision, or environmental factors. Evaluation identifies the functional problems that should guide treatment.

conditions.title: Gait and Walking Difficulty
conditions.summary: Walking difficulty may involve strength, coordination, balance, endurance, pain, sensation, or confidence.

conditions.title: Weakness and Deconditioning
conditions.summary: Illness, hospitalization, inactivity, and chronic conditions can reduce strength, endurance, and confidence with everyday movement.

conditions.title: Loss of Everyday Independence
conditions.summary: Changes in mobility, cognition, vision, sensation, or endurance can make ordinary daily activities difficult.

conditions.title: Developmental Delay
conditions.summary: Children may benefit from therapy when motor, communication, feeding, sensory, or daily-living skills are developing differently or more slowly than expected.

conditions.title: Sensory Difficulties
conditions.summary: Sensory differences can affect attention, regulation, play, dressing, feeding, and participation in daily routines.

conditions.title: Feeding Difficulties
conditions.summary: Feeding difficulties may involve oral-motor skills, sensory responses, coordination, swallowing, behavior, or positioning.

conditions.title: Communication Delay
conditions.summary: Children may need support with understanding language, expressing themselves, speech clarity, social communication, or communication devices.

conditions.title: Motor and Coordination Difficulties
conditions.summary: Motor difficulties may affect sitting, standing, walking, hand use, play, school activities, or self-care.

conditions.title: Back and Neck Pain
conditions.summary: Back and neck pain may affect movement, sleep, work, exercise, and confidence with activity. Rehabilitation should focus on the person’s functional limitations rather than generic promises of a cure.

conditions.title: Joint and Extremity Pain
conditions.summary: Shoulder, arm, hand, hip, knee, ankle, or foot problems can limit strength, mobility, work, self-care, and recreation.

conditions.title: Persistent or Chronic Pain
conditions.summary: Persistent pain often affects movement, sleep, endurance, mood, and participation. Rehabilitation may use graded activity, education, movement retraining, and practical adaptation.

conditions.title: Post-Surgical Rehabilitation
conditions.summary: Rehabilitation after surgery is based on the procedure, medical precautions, current function, and the goals established with the patient and referring clinician.

conditions.title: Work, Motor-Vehicle & Sports Injuries
conditions.summary: Injuries may require a structured return to movement, work, driving, exercise, or recreation.
